Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
1008 PM PST Mon Nov 23 2026

UPDATED AVIATION SECTION

.SYNOPSIS...23/331 PM.

Mild and dry conditions are expected into Tuesday except for some
cold overnight temperatures. Light rain is possible again Tuesday
night into Wednesday along the Central coast. Thanksgiving and 
Friday will be warm and dry. A cooling trend will begin over the 
weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM (MON-THU)...23/930 PM.

***UPDATE***

Today was relatively uneventful with some lingering morning clouds
over interior San Luis Obispo County and portions of western 
Santa Barbara County. Highs ranged from the 50s to low 60s for the
interior and north of Point Conception, with warmer mid to upper 
60s for the southern coasts and valleys. This evening, light 
offshore winds have developed and are forecast to strengthen into 
Tuesday morning. Winds should remain below advisory levels, but 
higher topography like the Santa Susana Mountains, San Gabriel 
Mountains, and portions of the Ventura County Mountains could see 
gusts around 30 to 35 mph at times. These offshore winds paired 
with ridging will bring 5 to 10 degrees of warming for Tuesday. 
Still expecting a front to approach the region from the northwest 
Tuesday night into early Wednesday, however most recent high 
resolution guidance shows rain showers struggling to reach the 
coast. May need to cut back on the coverage of rain chances, but 
will wait to see if future guidance still sticks with this 
solution before adjusting. While we may not see much difference in
temperatures Tuesday to Wednesday, Thursday shows significant 
warming with stronger offshore flow. Highs could reach the mid 70s
to low 80s throughout the coastal valleys and coasts. Although 
warm conditions generally encourage folks to flock to the 
beaches, very high tides, large surf and the significant threat of
coastal flooding will make for problematic beach weather 
Wednesday and Thursday (see beaches section for more information).

***From Previous Discussion***

For the most part this will be a dry week with increasing offshore
flow and warming temperatures. The main caveat to that being
Tuesday night when the tail end of a storm moving into the Pac NW
and approaches SLO County. Models have backed off quite a bit on
rain chances there and any rain amounts would be very light and 
with very minimal impact. Clouds will eventually cover most of the
area Tuesday night into early Wednesday morning but sunny skies 
expected the rest of Wednesday.

In the meantime, offshore gradients are expected to be increasing
this week, starting Tuesday with gusts to around 30 mph from  
Santa Clarita and the surrounding mountains through the 126 
corridor and into the Oxnard plain, as well as the northwest San 
Fernando Valley. Winds expected to remain below advisory levels.

The return of offshore flow will start a warming trend that will
last through the week, conveniently peaking on Thanksgiving.
However, winds will increasing as well, possibly enough for some 
low end wind advisories in the above areas. The warmest 
temperatures will be at the coast and in the coastal valleys with 
highs in the upper 70s to mid 80s. The higher valleys and interior
areas will be cooler which is typical in offshore conditions.

.LONG TERM (FRI-MON)...23/225 PM.

Dry weather will continue at least through Saturday, though
temperatures will be cooling, especially for coast and valleys as
pressure gradients trend strongly onshore in response to the next
storm system moving into the Pac NW. That system will move through
the area mostly on Sunday. Most areas will get at least some light
rain, but more so along the Central Coast where up to an inch
could fall, especially the northern portion. Rain amounts south of
Pt Conception will be quite a bit less, likely under a half inch.

At least one more storm is expected next week, around Tuesday with
the possibility of 1-3 inches in upslope areas.

&&

.AVIATION...24/0608Z.

At 0533Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, high confidence in VFR TAFs except at KPRB where
LIFR to VLIFR conditions are expected late tonight through
early Tuesday morning. Timing of CIG/VSBY restrictions may 
be off +/- 2 hours from current forecast. There is also a 
15% chance of LIFR to VLIFR conditions at KSBP from 09Z-16Z.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Any east wind component
is expected to remain below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF. No wind issues expected.

&&

.MARINE...23/745 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. High confidence in winds and seas remaining below Small
Craft Advisory (SCA) levels through Tuesday afternoon. From 
Tuesday night through Thursday night, high confidence in 
combination of Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level winds and seas. 
Seas during this period will peak between 14 and 18 feet on 
Wednesday and Wednesday night. For Friday through Saturday, high 
confidence in winds remaining below SCA levels, but a 60-80% 
chance of SCA level seas.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through Tuesday, high confidence 
in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For Tuesday night 
through Thursday night, high confidence in combination of SCA 
level winds and seas. Seas during this period will peak between 13
and 16 feet on Wednesday. For Friday through Saturday, high 
confidence in winds remaining below SCA levels, but a 40-60% 
chance of SCA level seas. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through Tuesday night, high 
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For 
Wednesday, there is a 50-60% chance of SCA level winds across the 
western half of the Santa Barbara Channel and a 30-40% chance of 
SCA level seas. For Thursday, there is a 50-70% chance of SCA 
level northeast winds from Ventura to Santa Monica and a 40-60% 
chance of SCA level seas. For Friday through Saturday, high 
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels.

&&

.BEACHES...23/752 PM.

A large, long period, west swell will move into the coastal
waters on Tuesday and peak on Wednesday and Thursday. This large
swell will combine with very high tides to bring significant surf
to the area as well as significant coastal flooding.

The highest surf and most significant coastal flooding issues are
expected across the Central Coast as well as the beaches of
Ventura county. Elsewhere, the surf and coastal flooding issues
are a bit less, but still concerning. There will be many, strong
rip currently nearly everywhere, strong long shore currents, a
risk of sneaker waves, large shore pound, coastal erosion and
potential for breaking waves in the harbor entrances. 

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories and warnings in effect.
